change_summary: The PLOS ONE Editors issued an Expression of Concern about this paper to inform readers of unresolved issues, and the authors did not respond or could not be reached. The notice reports an apparent vertical discontinuity in the Fig. 4 LSD1 panel between the 293T and A549 lanes, while the paper uses Figure 4's lower LSD1 level in A549 than in H460 as the basis for transfecting Flag-LSD1 into A549 and LSD1 siRNA into H460. The notice also says Fig. 7 reports no LSD1 siRNA data, so the paper's statement that LSD1 siRNA reduced migration of H460 cells is unsupported, and that the paper does not describe the controls in the transfection experiments well enough to replicate them. Those experiments sit behind the abstract's report that LSD1 siRNA or pargyline suppressed proliferation, migration and invasion, and that LSD1 over-expression enhanced cell growth. The notice says similarities with other research groups' work call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, but it does not say which results, so the paper's findings are in doubt, particularly the cell-line experiments, but the notice does not retract them.
evaluation: In Section 3, your draft cites Lv et al. [12] for a scratch assay in which LSD1 siRNA reduced migration of H460 cells and Flag-LSD1 increased migration of A549 cells (their Figure 7), and calls this single cell-line study the main evidence for its hypothesis. The notice says Fig. 7 reports no LSD1 siRNA data, so the statement that LSD1 siRNA reduced H460 migration is not supported, and it says the paper does not describe the controls in the Flag-LSD1 and LSD1 siRNA transfection experiments well enough to replicate them, so the Section 3 use is touched. In its Background section, your draft also cites Lv et al. [12] for LSD1 being higher in lung cancer tissue and linked to shorter survival, and whether that use is touched is unclear: the notice says similarities with other groups' work call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, but it does not say which results. The change is an Expression of Concern issued to inform readers of unresolved issues, and the authors did not respond or could not be reached, so the impact on the draft is medium.

alerts.what_changed: PLOS ONE issued an Expression of Concern about this paper. It flags an apparent splice in the Fig. 4 LSD1 blot and says Fig. 7 has no siRNA data behind a stated migration result. It also says the control details for the transfection experiments are too thin to replicate them, and that similarities with other groups' work call into question the validity and provenance of the results. The authors did not respond.

The notice reports an apparent vertical discontinuity in the Fig. 4 LSD1 panel between the 293T and A549 lanes, while the paper uses Figure 4's lower LSD1 level in A549 than in H460 as the basis for transfecting Flag-LSD1 into A549 and LSD1 siRNA into H460.

The notice also says Fig. 7 reports no LSD1 siRNA data, so the paper's statement that LSD1 siRNA reduced migration of H460 cells is unsupported, and that the paper does not describe the controls in the transfection experiments well enough to replicate them. Those experiments sit behind the abstract's report that LSD1 siRNA or pargyline suppressed proliferation, migration and invasion, and that LSD1 over-expression enhanced cell growth.

The notice says similarities with other research groups' work call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, but it does not say which results, so the paper's findings are in doubt, particularly the cell-line experiments, but the notice does not retract them.
